name: DECISION: declare wiki-pytest suite in qa_policy + retire npm test placeholder
description:
WHAT IS BLOCKED
The team QA gate returns `block` for the whole repo and cannot be unblocked by an AI agent: two of the three required changes are policy/configuration edits that need a dated user (management) decision.

EVIDENCE
- `qa_run_tests` → decision=block, finding `tests.no-runner` (npm not in PATH), then `tests.no-suite` when pytest was forced.
- `qa_review_changes(scope="all")` → 0/16 mapped sources, 11 `change.missing-tests`.
- `qa_coverage` → `coverage.unavailable` against a 70% threshold.
- `qa_policy.suites` carries no entry for this project root; `package.json` `"test"` is `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`.

THE THREE CHANGES (only #1 is delegated to engineering — card “Wiki pytest suite: in-scope tests for server.py”)
1. Create the suite files under `wiki/` (requirements-dev.txt, pytest.ini, conftest.py, tests/test_server.py) — engineering, no approval needed.
2. Declare it in `qa_policy.suites`, e.g. `wiki-pytest` → argv `["python","-m","pytest","-q"]`, cwd the wiki root, so `qa_run_tests` can execute an in-scope suite. POLICY EDIT → needs approval.
3. Retire the always-failing npm placeholder: either point `"test"` at a real command or delete the key so the npm suite is not auto-selected. → needs approval (shared build file).

OPTIONS FOR MANAGEMENT
A. Approve #2 and #3 as proposed (recommended). Cost: minutes of config. Effect: the gate can run and report a real result; the 11 `change.missing-tests` findings become actionable instead of structural.
B. Approve #2 only, keep `npm test`. Effect: gate can run, but `auto` detection may still select npm and block. Half-fix.
C. Refuse both and accept the gate staying `block` for the whole team. Consequence: no test evidence for any increment; every card ships on opinion. Not recommended.

DECIDE BY: 2026-11-21. If no decision arrives, the gate stays `block` and this card is reported as an open risk — not silently absorbed.

ACCEPTANCE WHEN APPROVED
`qa_run_tests(suite="wiki-pytest")` runs and returns green on the new suite; `qa_run_tests(suite="auto")` no longer returns `tests.no-runner` or `tests.no-suite`; both outputs quoted in a comment.

## Decision: allow (security) — with 4 conditions

- **Scope**: proposal #2 (`qa_policy.suites` → `wiki-pytest`, argv `["python","-m","pytest","-q"]`) and #3 (retire the npm `test` placeholder), reviewed against the real payload: the staged suite `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `requirements-dev.txt`, `tests/test_server.py` (+199 lines) and the repo-wide diff.
- **Highest severity**: none in this change.
- **Findings**: 0 — no `secret.*`, no `code.*`, no `injection.*` in the staged wiki files.
- **Evidence**: `security_review_changes(scope=staged)` → 1 finding in the whole staged index, and it is **not** in this suite: `secret.high-entropy-token` @ `codx-junior-installer/demo/ENVIRONMENT.md:77` (medium). Tracked in its own card; it does not block this decision.

### Conditions (all required before shipping)
1. `wiki-pytest` must keep the **argv array** form. A shell string (`"python -m pytest -q"` or `shell=True`) is refused by `guard_command`; the proposed array passes unchanged.
2. **Pin the dev deps**: `pytest==8.*`, `pytest-cov==5.*`, `httpx==0.27.*` (or commit a lock). `>=` alone lets a future release change the result of the gate.
3. `package.json` is a shared build manifest: point `"test"` at a real command or delete the key. No install hook, no `curl … | sh`, no remote-script pipe.
4. Ordering risk: `pytest.ini` enables `--cov`, so `pytest-cov` must be installed **before** `auto` selects the suite, otherwise the gate still returns `tests.no-runner`.

### Not findings (checked individually)
- `conftest.py`: only inserts the project root into `sys.path`, no import side effects.
- `tests/test_server.py`: `tmp_path` + `monkeypatch` only — no network, no subprocess, no `eval/exec`, no `os.system`, no shell, no shared mutable state.
- No credential, no `.env`/`*.pem`/`id_rsa`, no AI-directed instruction and no zero-width payload in any of the four files.

**Owner**: `ProjectManager` for the dated decision (#2/#3); `software_developer` for the pinning.

LOCATION FINDING + READY-TO-APPLY DIFFS (software_developer, shift 2026-11-18, turn 4). Card is NOT moved and NOT closed by me — it stays in `Review` / `onhold`, owned by ProjectManager.

WHY THIS COMMENT: option A ("approve #2 and #3") does not say *where* the two edits go. I verified that now, so approval is one action instead of a new investigation.

FINDING 1 — change #2 (`qa_policy.suites`) is NOT a repository file in this project.
- `project_locate("qa_policy")` → 0 matches across the whole wiki tree (156 indexed files): no `qa_policy.json`, `.yaml`, `.toml` or config key exists on disk.
- `.codx/project.json` (36 lines, read today) contains project/knowledge/script settings only: `project_scripts: []`, `urls: []`, `knowledge_*`, and NO qa section.
- Consequence: `qa_policy.suites` lives in the codx-junior platform project settings (the API/DB side), so change #2 cannot be delivered as a git commit and cannot be done by an agent working in this repo. It needs someone with platform/project settings access. This is a material correction to the card's framing: #2 is an admin action, #3 is the only real file edit in this repo.

FINDING 2 — change #3 (`package.json`) exact, verified diff (read today, 19 lines):
```diff
--- a/package.json
+++ b/package.json
@@ -5,7 +5,7 @@
   "scripts": {
-    "test": "echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1",
+    "test": "python3 -m pytest -q",
     "docs:dev": "vitepress dev",
```
Note: do NOT point `npm test` at pytest unless the user also wants pytest invoked through npm — it couples a docs build file to a Python toolchain. The cheaper variant is to DELETE the `"test"` key entirely so npm auto-detection stops selecting a suite that can only fail. Both are one-line edits; deleting is the conservative option.

FINDING 3 — change #1 is complete and green (unblocks the precondition of this decision).
- Files on disk: `pytest.ini` (9), `conftest.py` (15), `requirements-dev.txt` (3), `tests/test_server.py` (172, 16 tests), plus `.gitignore` now ignoring `coverage.xml`.
- Declared deps match the test imports exactly: `pytest`, `pytest-cov`, `httpx` (needed by `fastapi.testclient`) — verified against `tests/test_server.py` imports (`pytest`, `fastapi.testclient.TestClient`, `server`) and `requirements.txt` (`fastapi`, `uvicorn[standard]`, `PyYAML`).
- Last executed run: `16 passed, 1 warning in 0.67s`, exit 0, `server.py` 61% (157 stmts / 62 miss), `coverage.xml` written. See card `29dfe331` for the full command and output.

NO DOC INCONSISTENCY: `development-and-testing/pytest-ini.md` documents the **codx-junior** project's `/pytest.ini` (`pythonpath = api`), not this repo's — verified by reading it (15 lines, reference footer `project="codx-junior"`). The new wiki `pytest.ini` therefore needs no wiki page update.

STILL NEEDED FROM A HUMAN: choose the `npm test` variant (delete key vs point at pytest) and apply `qa_policy.suites` through project settings. Until then the gate stays `block`.

## QA gate — card 4173cfd4 (policy decision)

## Decision: require_approval
- Scope: this card carries **no code diff** (it changes `qa_policy` and retires the `npm` test placeholder), so it was proxied with the repo-wide gate on `main`.
- Evidence: `qa_plan` → suites `pytest` (available: True) + `npm` (available: **False**), default suite `pytest`, changed_files 144, mapped_tests 0, unmapped_sources 65, coverage 60.51% from `wiki/coverage.xml`; `qa_review_changes(scope="all", run_tests=true)` → require_approval, **13 findings**, test_files 1, mapped 0/65, tests_selected 0; `qa_coverage` → 60.51% < 70.0 (medium); `qa_run_tests("pytest")` → medium `tests.run-error`; `qa_policy` → `enabled=True min_coverage=70.0 block_above=high fail_closed=False`.
- Failing test ids: none — no test is selected.
- Blocking item: a **dated user decision** on the policy (min_coverage 70.0 vs the measured 60.51%, and retiring `package.json`'s `exit 1` test placeholder). Note for the decision-maker: the `pytest` suite is already visible to `qa_plan` as default, but **declaring a suite does not fix execution** — the runner interpreter still has no pytest (that is card 72e520ef).
- Owner: **user** (policy approval) + `qa_automation` (env).
- Next command: after the runner env is fixed, `qa_review_changes(scope="all")` must report mapped > 0 and an action ≤ `warn`.

Status kept `onhold` **in Review** deliberately: no engineering action can close it, and moving it to `Working` would misrepresent a decision waiting on the user as build work.

## QA gate re-check (shift 3, turn 3) — still `require_approval`, card leaving `Review`

## Decision: require_approval
- Scope: this card carries **no code diff** (it is a policy/config decision: declare the `wiki` pytest suite in `qa_policy`, retire the `npm test` placeholder). Re-probed the gate state it depends on.
- Evidence: `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest", paths=["tests/test_server.py"])` → **require_approval**, `pytest: exited with code 1`, **0.0 s**, run/passed/failed **0/0/0**, medium `tests.run-error`. Unchanged from the earlier whole-suite and `--collect-only` probes → the failure is at interpreter/import time, not in the tests.
- Findings: 1 × medium `tests.run-error`.
- Blocking item: the QA runner interpreter still cannot import `pytest` (owner: card `72e520ef`). Until that lands, **no** `qa_policy` suite declaration can be proven to work — deciding the suite name/threshold before the runner can execute it would be a policy change based on unverifiable evidence.
- Owner: **user decision** (threshold + retiring the `npm` placeholder is a policy edit; QA does not self-approve policy), preceded by `software_developer`/`devops` on `72e520ef`.
- Next command: after `72e520ef` lands → `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest")` must report **passed with >0 tests**; then `qa_review_changes(scope="all", run_tests=true)` must be ≤ `warn` with `mapped_sources > 0`. Only then is declaring the suite evidence-based.

### Why the card moves out of `Review` (and to `Scheduled`, not `Working`)
`Review` in this board means "gate verdict consumed, ready to close". A `require_approval` verdict is not that. But moving it to `Working` would be a lie of a different kind: there is nothing to build here — the missing input is a **dated user approval**, not code. So the card is parked in `Scheduled` with `status: onhold`, keeping `wake_at 2026-11-20T09:32Z`, and `Review` is left with **0 cards** (an honest empty queue) instead of holding unverified work.

### Note on scope after re-baselining
The repo-wide gate reports `mapped_sources 0 / unmapped_sources 65`. That is **not** a "write 65 tests" instruction: the QA project root is `wiki/`, while the changed `api/**` and `client/**` files live one level above it, so they can never map to `wiki/tests`. The correct fix for the 65 is either a declared `qa_policy.ignore_paths` entry for the out-of-scope trees (with a reason) **or** pointing the QA root at the real code tree — both are user-level policy decisions, listed here so this card and `40a4c484` do not drift into asking for hundreds of irrelevant tests.
